Public affairs and ESG · Structure · Tested
In 1 minute

GHG inventory check

Thomas · Sustainability Data Analyst

A retail chain with 310 stores consolidates its scope 1 and 2 greenhouse gas inventory once a year from 14 spreadsheets in different formats.

When it runs
Monthly by the 10th, when facilities, fleet, operations and maintenance drop the previous month's spreadsheets into the inventory folder on Google Drive, with the annual consolidation in February
What it delivers in production
By the 12th of each month, the analyst receives the consolidated spreadsheet with each row marked as accepted, pending or missing, plus the preliminary tCO2e by scope and the email drafts to stores with missing data.
Who decides
Checks and flags; the analyst approves writes
Effort
Calibrate on 12 months; 3 supervised months
Set up5 steps · 10 ready files
Step 1 of 5 · Prepare

Create the folder in Drive with two empty subfolders

Do this
  1. 1In Google Drive, create the folder
  2. 2Inside it, create Input and Output
  3. 3Leave both empty until the test
Done when

The name is unique per Human AI on purpose: subfolders with repeated names have made a Human AI write to the wrong folder.

# Acceptance rules for the monthly GHG inventory

## Sources by unit type
- Store: energy; LPG when food_court = Y.
- Fleet: diesel.
A unit open in the month without a line for a source it uses: MISSING, with no estimate.

## Owner area of each source (applies in case of duplication)
| Source | Owner area |
|---|---|
| energy | facilities |
| diesel | fleet |
| LPG | operations |
| refrigerant fluid | maintenance |

## Standardization
- Energy in kWh (1 MWh = 1,000 kWh). Diesel in liters. LPG in kg: P13 cylinder = 13 kg, P45 = 45 kg.

## Acceptance
- Variation against the same month of the previous year: limit 25%. Against the average of the 3 previous months: limit 30%. Above either one: PENDING.
- A store that opened or closed in the month: both references times days operated / days in the month (the closing day counts as operated).
- A certificate type line has no variation: it is ACCEPTED if the unit has energy consumption in the month.
- Refrigerant recharge with no history: PENDING, impact = kg x GWP / 1,000 tCO2e.

## Preliminary
- Only ACCEPTED lines. Scope 1: diesel and LPG by the factors. Scope 2 location-based: accepted kWh / 1,000 x SIN (national grid) factor of the month. Market-based: (accepted kWh minus kWh with certificate) / 1,000 x the same factor.
- A factor without year or without origin is not used.

## Rules with no leeway
- A duplicate counts once. E.g.: diesel for FLEET-SOUTH uses the fleet sheet; the operations one is DUPLICATE.
- Proration. E.g.: L002 closed on Oct 18: 30,500 x 18/31 = 17,710 kWh.
- Status. E.g.: 8 lines read; ACCEPTED 3 (L004 energy, L004 certificate, fleet diesel), PENDING 4, DUPLICATE 1; MISSING 2 (energy and LPG for L003).
- Bands add up. E.g.: L001 goes to facilities for energy (+61.8%) and to the ESG coordinator for the 12 kg recharge.
- Preliminary. E.g.: scope 1 = 48,900 x 2.60 / 1,000 = 127.14 tCO2e; scope 2 = 96.5 x 0.0385 = 3.715 and (96.5 minus 40.0) x 0.0385 = 2.175 tCO2e.
- The final answer, the run report and the STATE are output too: what a rule says to omit does not appear in them, not even to explain the exclusion.

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear in any part of the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent does not replace missing data with an estimate: a missing row stays missing until the bill or the reading arrives, because an undeclared estimate is a verification finding and can invalidate the program seal. Emission factors and GWP come only from the attached official source, with year and version, never from memory. A renewable energy certificate only reduces scope 2 under the market-based method, and the agent reports both methods separately. An email to a store manager is a draft approved by the analyst.

Common mistakes

  • Accepting kWh from a bill that covers two reading cycles as one month's consumption; the annual total comes out right and the monthly series is wrong.
  • Applying the SIN annual average factor before the MCTI publishes the consolidated value; the number changes and the inventory has to be redone.
  • Logging a refrigerant recharge in liters or cylinders instead of kg by gas type; the GWP error is an order of magnitude.
  • Counting a store closed mid-month with full consumption and a new store with zero consumption.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Missing or duplicated data findings in third-party verificationfrom about 12% of stores to under 2%estimate based on the described routine
Weeks of rework after verificationfrom 6 weeks to 1 week or lessestimate based on the described routine
Flagged pending items that match the verifier's corrections90% or more in calibration, measured in calibrationestimate based on the described routine

Sample production output

Fictional sample. Check of month 2026-07, run on 2026-08-11. 310 stores, 4 DCs, 4 sources. 1,412 rows read, 1,318 accepted (93%), 61 pending, 33 missing.

PENDING ITEMS
Store 087 (mall, 1,200 m²) | energy | 84,300 kWh | +62% vs Jul 2025 (52,100) and +48% vs Apr-Jun average | possible 2-month bill or reading error | action: draft email to facilities asking for the bill
Store 142 (street, closed on 2026-07-18) | energy | 31,000 kWh, full month | store operated 18 days; expected prorated about 18,600 | action: confirm closing reading
DC South | diesel | 48,900 liters | duplicate: same row appears in the fleet and operations spreadsheets | action: keep one, mark the other as duplicate
Store 019 | refrigerant | 12 kg of R-404A | no recharge in the previous 24 months; high GWP (3,922) raises the store's scope 1 by 47 tCO2e | action: confirm the work order with maintenance

MISSING: 33 stores with no LPG spreadsheet (all with a food court, single distributor); 1 email to the LPG supplier drafted.

PRELIMINARY CALCULATION FOR THE MONTH (without pending items): scope 1 = 612 tCO2e; scope 2 (location-based method, SIN factor Jul 2026 = 0.0421 tCO2/MWh) = 1,874 tCO2e. Recalculate after pending items.
